chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about an Imam who led a congregation in prayer, and it was mentioned that he had not been in a state of ablution (wudu). He then turned away, took a man by the hand, brought him in, and placed him forward, while the man who was placed forward did not know what the congregation had prayed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He prays with them. If he makes a mistake, the congregation will glorify (by saying SubhanAllah) to remind him, and he will build upon the prayer of the one who was before him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an Imam leads prayer without ablution and realizes it later?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Imams (peace be upon them) clarifies the validity of the congregation's prayer when the Imam leads without ablution, establishing that the Imam can seamlessly take over from a layperson to complete the prayer. It highlights the Shia principle of 'building upon' (bina') the previous actions, ensuring the prayer remains valid even if the Imam errs, provided the congregation corrects him. This ruling underscores the flexibility and continuity of communal worship in Shia jurisprudence.
